tweets: Missing or insufficient access controls allow malicious parties to withdraw some or all Ether from a contract account.
This risk can stem from unintentionally exposing initialization functions that lack proper protection.
By wrongly naming a function intended to be a constructor, the constructor code ends up in runtime bytecode.
Anyone can then call that exposed constructor to re-initialize the contract and drain funds.
Check for exposed initialization functions during your review process.
Verify that constructor logic remains protected from external invocation.
